preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit() and len(line.split()) == 3) and all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for x in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit() and len(line.split()) == 3])
preconditions.description: The first line contains integers n (number of cities), m (number of roads), and s (capital city), where 2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5, 1 ≤ s ≤ n, and m is implied by the number of road lines.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()[:2]) and 1 <= int(line.split()[2]) <= 1000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:-1])
preconditions.description: Each of the m road lines contains three integers vi, ui, wi (1 ≤ vi, ui ≤ n, vi ≠ ui, 1 ≤ wi ≤ 1000), representing bidirectional roads between cities with their lengths.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(line) <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines()[-1:])
preconditions.description: The last line contains integer l (0 ≤ l ≤ 10^9), the distance from the capital to the missile silos.
The input consists of exactly m + 2 lines: one for n, m, s; m lines for roads; and one for l.

preconditions.expression: all(vi != ui for vi, ui, _ in (tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:-1]))
preconditions.description: No road connects a city to itself.

preconditions.expression: any(all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in [int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:-1])
preconditions.description: All cities referenced in roads exist (1 ≤ vi, ui ≤ n).

postconditions.description: The output is a single non-negative integer representing the total number of missile silos located in Berland.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout.strip()) <= n + sum(int(line.split()[2]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:-1]))
postconditions.description: The output count is bounded by the maximum possible silos: cities (n) plus all possible points on roads (sum of all road lengths).

postconditions.expression: let cities = {int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:-1]} | {int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:-1]}; let roads = [(tuple(map(int, line.split()[:2])), int(line.split()[2])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:-1]]; let s = int(stdin.splitlines()[0].split()[2]); let l = int(stdin.splitlines()[-1]); let graph = {u: {v: w for v, w in [(vi, wi) if vi != s else (ui, wi) for vi, ui, wi in roads]} for u in cities}; let distances = {s: 0}; let queue = [s]; let visited = {s}; let parent = {s: None}; let edge_parent = {}; let edge_dist = {}; while queue: u = queue.pop(0); for v, w in graph[u].items(): if v not in visited: visited.add(v); distances[v] = distances[u] + w; parent[v] = u; queue.append(v); for (u1, u2), w in roads: if u1 in visited and u2 in visited: if distances[u1] + w < distances[u2]: distances[u2] = distances[u1] + w; parent[u2] = u1; elif distances[u2] + w < distances[u1]: distances[u1] = distances[u2] + w; parent[u1] = u2; let silos = 0; for city in cities: if distances[city] == l: silos += 1; for (u1, u2), w in roads: if distances[u1] == l or distances[u2] == l: continue; if distances[u1] < l < distances[u2] or distances[u2] < l < distances[u1]: silos += 1; if distances[u1] == l or distances[u2] == l: silos += 1; return int(stdout.strip()) == silos
postconditions.description: The output count equals the number of missile silos located either in cities or on roads at exactly distance l from the capital. A silo is counted in a city if its shortest distance from the capital is exactly l. A silo is counted on a road between cities u1 and u2 if the shortest distance from the capital to some point on the road is exactly l, which happens if l lies strictly between the distances of u1 and u2 or exactly matches one of them (in which case the silo is at the endpoint).
